title: Solo mining, pools, and Stratum
outcome: Trace one job from the pool to a miner and one share back.
show: Draw a pool-to-miner arrow labeled job and a miner-to-pool arrow labeled share. Add a second checkpoint for the stricter network target.
concepts: A solo miner seeks a valid block and receives block rewards if that block is accepted and the miner controls the coinbase payout.
A pool tracks contributed work with shares that meet its own target. Pool-specific terms govern payment. A qualifying share also meets the network target only when it is low enough.
Stratum carries work and share submissions. Stratum V2 has a public specification and open-source reference implementation. Firmware and pool support determine what can connect.
replicate: Use hypothetical pool and network targets of 50 and 5. Sort values 3, 8, and 60 into both targets, only pool target, or neither.
Mark the difference between an accepted share, a valid block, and a payout in the diagram.
check: What does an accepted share prove?
The pool acknowledged qualifying work under its share and job rules. The share alone establishes neither a block nor a payout.

challenge.title: Run the pool’s share desk
challenge.prompt: The pool target is 50. The network target is 5. Classify each candidate hash.
cards: 8 is at or below 50 and above 5.
3 meets both numeric targets. The network still checks the rest of the block.
challenge.tip: Meeting the pool’s target records work for the pool. A network target can be stricter.
